ABSTRACT
INTRODUCTION
Optimalintraoperativeandpostoperativepainmanagementis criticalto achievepositivepatient outcomes,as it notonlyamelioratespatientdiscomfortbutalsoenablesan objective
assessmentof pain. Althoughthesurgicalplethindex(SPI; GE Healthcare,Chicago,IL,USA)is a frequentlyemployedpainassessmenttool,itsuseis notrecommendedforconscious
patients,andnopainevaluationtechniquehasbeenreportedtobeeffectiveinmeasuringbothintraoperativeandpostoperativepain. Therefore,thepurposeofthisstudyistodevelop
a novelpainassessmenttechniquethatcanbeappliedtobothperioperativeandpostoperativepain.
Thisstudyaimedto developa newpainassessmenttechniquethatcouldbe usedforevaluatingbothintra- andpost-operativepain. Photoplethysmogramwasanalyzedbefore,during,
and aftersurgeryto extract174 candidateindicatorsfor pain. We usedXGBoostmodelto selectthe mostimportantindicatorsfor discriminatingintra- and post-operativepainand
traineda comprehensivemodelfor painevaluation. The modelwas developedand validatedusing242 patientsundergeneralanesthesia. Painpresencewas labeledas “absent”or
“present”withrespecttointraoperativeandpostoperativepain. Theprimaryevaluationmetricusedwastheareaunderthecurveofthereceiveroperatingcharacteristiccurve(AUROC).
The developedmodelachievedan AUROCof 0.812 for classifyingintraoperativepain and an AUC of 0.768 for classifyingpostoperativepain. Comparedto SPI's0.822 and 0.577,
respectively,proposedmodelshowedsimilarperformanceinclassifyingpainduringsurgeryandsuperiorperformanceinclassifyingpostoperativepain.

(4) Preprocessing of PPG
• Filtering : 0.5-50 Hz FIR bandpass filter
• Peak detection : Adaptive threshold algorithm [1] and Manual correction 
(5) Feature extraction
• Basic features (25) : related to pulse interval, amplitude and slope.
• Normalized features (33) :calculating the ratio between basic features.
• Final analysis features (174 = 58 features x 3 representative values)

mance of the developed pain assessment model and SPI for intraoperative pain 
(A) and postoperative pain (B) assessments. 
The black curve represents the ROC curve of the developed model, and the red curve represents the ROC curve of SPI. The 
shaded area indicates the range of the ROC curve in 5-fold cross-validation. The cross (‘+’) indicates the optimal cut-off 
value, which is the point on the ROC curve with the minimum distance to the upper left corner.
DISCUSSION & CONCLUSION
REFERENCES
The resultsof this study suggestthat the newly developedpain evaluationtechnique
exhibitssimilarperformanceto conventionalSPI in classifyingpain duringsurgery,while
alsooutperformingitinidentifyingpostoperativepain.
These resultsare importantfor effectivepain managementduring and after surgery
becausethe developedmodelcan be a valuabletool for improvingpatientoutcomesby
alleviatingpatientdiscomfortandenablinganobjectiveevaluationofpain.
Figure 4. Histogram of the results of pain assessments. 
A and B represent the pain scores of the proposed model for intraoperative and postoperative pain, respectively. C and D 
represent the Surgical Pleth Index (SPI) for intraoperative and postoperative pain, respectively. The red bars indicate the 
pain group scores, while the blue bars indicate the non-pain group scores. The thick red and blue lines represent the mean 
scores of the pain and non-pain groups, respectively. The dotted lines indicate the cut-off value used as a decision 
boundary.
